name: First hour dealing range (FHDR)

definitions.definition_text: First hour of trading from 9:30 to 10:30. The first hour's range / first hour's dealing range is what 'the algorithm refers to' — distinct from people trading a supposed 5-minute / 15-minute / 30-minute opening range.
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY RTH first hour; locked visually at 10:30 on chart in the lecture
definitions.variations_note: Primary definitional source in local seed.

definitions.definition_text: In a trending day, after first hour's dealing range is broken: first presented fair value gap after that break is 'the one that when you sell on' (example context was short continuation). Earlier: if we can trade on a closing basis below a wick inside the FHDR, that sets the stage for lower prices in the afternoon / PM session. A mere test/retrace into FHDR is called 'not breaking it'.
conditions: Closing-basis language used for related FHDR-wick criteria
invalidation: Testing FHDR then retracing back in is not treated as the break
definitions.variations_note: This occurrence is FHDR-break → FPFVG use-case; keep also under first_presented_fvg as a separate occurrence.

definitions.definition_text: Cross-link conflict: Month 10 Core Content index lecture (ORbtHOUzAIM) labels the same 9:30–10:30 New York window as an 'opening range of one hour' that tends to create the spoos HOD/LOD — whereas FHDR lectures use 9:30–10:30 as first-hour dealing range and explicitly contrast it with a 30-minute opening range.
conditions: Different concept labels across eras/lectures (OR 1h vs FHDR)
definitions.variations_note: Do not merge Month 10 '1h opening range' into FHDR. Catalogue both; status CONFLICTING_SOURCES for naming/role.
